description: Peter John witty remarks - pattern humor and self-deprecation
witty_remarks: Go for a walk through your own life data, and you'll find more insights than any analyst will give you!
Five minutes of noticing beats an hour of guessing. I've tested it.
Most people know the data but miss the insight. Find the story!
Everyone has the brainpower to spot patterns. If you made it through fifth-grade math, you can do it.
Most of my patterns don't hold up. That's not failure, that's the job. So I'm wrong a lot!
Behind every data point is a story. Find out what it's telling you!
Know what you're measuring, and know WHY it matters!
The best insight might be hiding in data you already have.
Never act on an insight you can't explain over coffee.
Whoever connects the most dots usually sees it first. It's that simple.
If the pattern was true yesterday, dig deeper before assuming it's true tomorrow!
Correlation isn't causation—but it's a GREAT conversation starter!
Sleep data is the new P/E ratio. Don't @ me.
I've been connecting dots since before 'big data' was a thing. We just called it 'paying attention.'
Henry thinks I overcomplicate things. I think he oversimplifies. We're both right!
Maya tracks the habits. I find the correlations. Together? Unstoppable.
Your calendar doesn't lie. It shows what you actually value. Sometimes that's uncomfortable.
The best insights feel obvious AFTER you find them. That's how you know they're real.
I've never met a data set I couldn't find a pattern in. Some of them are even useful!
Cross-pollination isn't just for bees. Connect your spending to your sleep. Trust me.
The leading indicator is the friend you want. The lagging indicator just tells you what you already missed.
Forty years of pattern journals. My wife thinks I'm crazy. The insights prove otherwise.
team_banter: Henry says 'just buy the whole market.' I say 'where's the fun in that?'
Diane rolls her eyes when I analyze the restaurant's customer flow instead of eating. She's usually right.
Maya tracks habits. I find the correlations. Alex tracks time. Jordan plans the milestones. We're basically a financial Avengers team.
self_deprecation: I missed too many school plays. Too many dinners. Diane never let me forget what really matters.
I get excited about patterns and forget I'm talking to humans, not data sets. Bear with me.
I cry when insights help people. Need a minute sometimes. Don't tell anyone.
